The Owner's Guide to EnPlace Pro

Set up the organization, get your prices matched, watch the money — and know exactly which screens your managers and chefs can and can't reach.

Desktop + phoneboth covered
01

What being the Owner means here

You're the only role that can shape the organization — and the only one who can lock everyone out of it

EnPlace Pro has three roles inside a restaurant group. Owner is the one with the keys: you create the organization, add restaurants, invite people, connect suppliers, decide which product comparison list everyone uses, and pay the bill.

Owner — you
Everything. Org settings, restaurants, team, billing, suppliers, matching, reports, and ordering.
Manager
Oversight: reports, history and lists. No New Order button and no supplier logins — but they can manage your team. Read the note below carefully.
Chef
Places orders at one restaurant. Connects their own supplier logins. No reports.
Watch out

The role split is not what most people assume. Internally the app calls owners and chefs operators — they can create and change operational data. Managers sit outside that group, so they get no + NEW ORDER button, no Price Check and no supplier-credential editing.

But “manager” is meaningfully more powerful than “read-only”, in three ways worth knowing before you hand out a manager seat:

1. On the Team screen a manager can invite people, change roles between Chef and Manager, reassign restaurants and remove members — everything you can do except Edit Organization.

2. Product Matching has no menu link for managers, but the pages themselves aren't locked. A manager who reaches the URL can edit matches at their own restaurant. Only promoting and demoting an org-wide list is owner-only.

3. A manager can open an existing draft batch from Order History with Return to Checkout and press the batch submit button — that particular action isn't operator-gated. They can't create an order, but they can send one a chef already built.

Tip

This guide covers the four suppliers your group uses — US Foods, Chef's Warehouse, What Chefs Want and Premiere Produce One. The app also ships a Sysco integration and an Email Suppliers section for vendors who only send PDF price lists; both work the same way but aren't covered here.

The setup order that works

  1. Create the organization
  2. Add your restaurants
  3. Invite your team
  4. Connect supplier logins at each restaurant
  5. Let the order guides import, then review product matching
  6. Promote one matched list org-wide (optional but recommended)
  7. Set order and case minimums
Tip

Steps 1–3 are enforced: until you have an organization, at least one restaurant and at least one team member or pending invite, the app shows you a setup checklist instead of the dashboard and keeps most of the interface greyed out.

02

Creating your organization

The container everything else lives inside

The organization is your restaurant group. Restaurants, team members, supplier connections, matched lists and billing all hang off it. You'll be its owner, and there can only be one owner — there's no way to invite a second.

  • Organization Name is usually the group or company name, not a single restaurant.
  • Address, city, state and ZIP are required; phone is optional.
  • You can change all of it later from the Team screen's Edit Organization button.
03

Adding your restaurants

Each one is a delivery address and a separate set of prices
Who can do this

Your avatar→Restaurants — owner only. Managers and chefs have no link, and the create/edit/delete actions bounce them back to the dashboard if they find the URL.

  1. Avatar menu → Restaurants → Add Location.
  2. Name it the way your team says it out loud — “Downtown Kitchen”, not “Store #2”.
  3. Fill in the full address; this is what suppliers deliver to.
  4. Tick Set as default location for your main site.
Watch out

Order minimums and delivery schedules are not on this form, which is where almost everyone looks for them. Minimums live on the Team screen in the Supplier Requirements grid (covered shortly) or on an individual credential's Edit form.

Tip

You can't delete your last remaining restaurant — the app just refuses and sends you back to the list without an error.

04

Inviting and managing your team

Roles, restaurant assignments, and how seats are billed

Inviting someone

  1. Your avatar→Team, then use the Invite Team Member panel on the right.
  2. Enter their email and choose Chef or Manager.
  3. Assign the restaurant(s) — a chef gets exactly one; a manager can have several.
  4. Press Send Invitation.
Tip

If the invitation email doesn't arrive, the Team screen prints the full accept URL underneath each pending invitation in grey. Copy it and send it however you like.

Changing someone after the fact

  • Make Manager / Make Chef flips a role immediately.
  • Assign Restaurants opens checkboxes — tick, then Save Assignments.
  • Remove deactivates the member and frees their seat.
  • There's no menu on your own row or on the owner row — you can't demote or remove yourself.

Seats and what they cost

RuleDetail
Included seats5 with the base plan
What counts as a seatEvery active non-owner member plus every pending invitation
Beyond 5$10/month each, billed as an overage on your subscription
At the limit without a subscriptionSend Invitation is disabled and an amber banner appears
Watch out

Pending invitations consume seats. If you're at the cap and someone never accepted, cancel the stale invitation to free the seat rather than paying for it.

05

Connecting suppliers

Per person, per supplier, per restaurant

Supplier credentials are the app's fuel: without them there are no prices, no order guides and no comparison. They're stored encrypted, and they're scoped tightly.

Why it works this way

A credential belongs to one user, at one supplier, at one restaurant. Your US Foods login at Downtown Kitchen is a different record from the same login at Midtown Bistro, and your chefs cannot see your credentials at all — they connect their own. This is deliberate: supplier accounts usually differ per site, and it keeps one person's password change from breaking everyone.

If you get stuck

This is the number one owner stumbling block. The whole Supplier Credentials page requires a specific restaurant in context. If you're in All Locations mode you'll be bounced to the dashboard with “Please select a specific restaurant from the dropdown above to access this page.” Pick a restaurant in the top-right dropdown first. The same rule blocks Product Matching, Price Check, Order Lists and New Order.

SupplierAuth typeWhat you enter
US Foods2FA onlyUser ID; a code is sent each login
Premiere Produce One2FA onlyEmail address; a code is sent each login
Chef's WarehousePasswordEmail + password
What Chefs WantPasswordEmail + password
  • Validate re-tests a connection (and triggers a fresh code on 2FA suppliers).
  • Import pulls that supplier's order guides in now rather than waiting for the overnight run.
  • Active + Disconnected is normal on 2FA suppliers — the login is fine, the browser session lapsed.
  • The small number box on each card sets the display order suppliers appear in across the app.
06

Order minimums and case minimums

The rules that decide whether an order can be submitted

Suppliers won't deliver below a dollar minimum, and some require a minimum number of cases. EnPlace Pro enforces both — an order under its supplier's minimum can't be submitted, by anyone.

Who can do this

Your avatar→Team → scroll to Supplier Requirements. The grid has one row per supplier and one column per restaurant, plus a Default column.

  1. Set a Default value to apply the same minimum everywhere.
  2. Or leave Default blank and set per-restaurant values individually.
  3. Values save the moment you type them — there's no Save button.
  4. Clearing a value (or setting 0) deletes the requirement entirely.
Watch out

Setting a Default locks every per-restaurant cell in that row and silently discards any per-location overrides you'd already entered. Decide which model you want before you start typing.

Tip

The grid only lists suppliers you have credentials for. No credentials, no grid — which looks like a missing feature but is just an empty state.

07

The guided tour

Twelve steps, and you can restart it any time

The owner flow runs twelve steps: a welcome, four setup steps (organization, restaurant, team, suppliers) with real forms embedded in the panel, then a tour of matching, promoting a list, order lists, placing an order, order history and reports.

  • ← Back steps backwards; the × dismisses the tour.
  • Your avatar→Restart Tour brings it back whenever you want.
  • It's desktop only — the tour doesn't run on a phone.
  • Steps you've already completed still appear; the tour never skips ahead.
08

Order guides

What the app pulls down from each supplier every night

An order guide is the supplier's own list of what you buy from them, with their prices. The app logs in and re-imports these on a schedule — supplier catalogs at about 2am Eastern, order guides at about 4am — and keeps the sessions alive in between.

Watch out

This overview screen is currently unreachable in the app. Its route now redirects straight to Supplier Credentials, and nothing links to it. It's shown here because it's the clearest picture of how guides and sync status relate — but in practice you manage all of this from Supplier Credentials, where each card carries its own Import button. Individual guide pages still load if you have the URL.

StatusMeaning
Up to DateLast sync succeeded
Updating…A sync is running — takes 5–10 minutes; the page auto-refreshes
FailedThe scrape failed; usually a credential problem
PendingNever synced yet
Tip

You don't need to wait for the overnight job — press Import on a supplier's card in Supplier Credentials to pull that supplier's guides now. A sync-everything button exists in the code (and is smart enough to use one credential per supplier so it never double-scrapes the same account), but it currently has no reachable button in the interface.

09

Product matching

The single most valuable thing you'll set up

Matching is what turns four supplier catalogs into one comparison. It decides that US Foods' Spring Mix 3/2 LB and What Chefs Want's Spring Mix 6/1 LB are the same product — and once you confirm a match, it holds forever, including when you add a new supplier later.

Reading the counters

CounterWhat it meansWhat to do
Total ProductsEvery line on the list—
MatchedLines the app has resolved — automatically, or by your handThese are the ones being compared across suppliers
UnmatchedLines it couldn't resolveWork through these — each one is a price you're not comparing

Click a product's left cell to open the editor: rename the canonical product, choose which supplier's photo represents it, reassign or clear a supplier's item, or remove the line entirely.

Cleaning up

  • Duplicates usually appear when a supplier renames items in their order guide.
  • Bulk merge only touches machine-created lines — matches you edited by hand are never overwritten.
  • Sync New Products pulls in items that appeared in a guide since the list was built.
  • Re-match All deletes every existing match, including your manual work. It warns you once, and the warning is accurate — this cannot be undone.
10

Promoting a list org-wide

One canonical comparison for everybody

Each restaurant can have its own matched list, or you can promote one to be the organization default — the list every chef and manager at every restaurant sees.

Per-restaurant listsOne promoted org-wide list
Best whenSites buy genuinely different thingsSites buy broadly the same things
MaintenanceOnce per restaurantOnce, ever
ConsistencyPrices can be matched differently per siteEveryone compares identically
Watch out

Promoting makes the list read-only for everyone, including you. The edit controls disappear and the list shows a purple Org-Wide badge. To change anything you have to Demote from Org-Wide first, edit, then promote again. This surprises owners who think their permissions have broken.

Watch out

Only one list can be the organization default at a time, and promoting a second one is refused rather than swapped — you get an error saying another list is already promoted. Demote from Org-Wide on the current one first.

11

Your dashboard

Where the money went, this month
PanelWhat it shows
Hero tileAll-time savings across every order the organization has placed
Stat cardsSpend and savings this month with month-over-month change, team size, restaurant count
Weekly SpendingEight weeks of spend
Team ActivityOrders and spend per person this month — each row links to that person's report
Restaurant PerformanceSpend and savings per restaurant — each row links to that restaurant's report
Supplier ConnectionsLive status of every credential you hold
If you get stuck

All Locations is a viewing mode, not a working mode. While it's selected, the app deliberately disables everything operational: + NEW ORDER greys out with the tooltip “Select a specific restaurant”, the Order Lists, Menu Planner and Price Check links disappear from the nav entirely, and Supplier Credentials and Product Matching refuse to load if you reach them another way. Reports and Team keep working — they're the two things designed for the org-wide view.

Two alerts can appear above the stat cards, and both matter:

Tip

The off-list alert is a to-do list, not a telling-off. Each item arrived with exactly one supplier attached and no comparison — matching it to competing suppliers is how it starts saving money next time. Chefs never see this alert, so it's on you and your managers.

12

Reports

The number that pays for the software
Watch out

The default range is the last 30 days, not month-to-date. That's why the totals here won't match your dashboard's “this month” figures. Choose the This Month preset to line them up.

  • Presets cover Last 30/60/90 Days plus This/Last Month, Quarter and Year — picking one auto-applies.
  • Every row in every table is clickable and drills through, carrying your filters with it.
  • Only completed orders count. Drafts, failed and unresolved price-changed orders are invisible here.
  • The restaurant dropdown in the top nav also scopes reports — check it if numbers look small.

The two savings screens

Why it works this way

These are two different questions. Product Savings is retrospective and real: what you paid versus the most expensive matched option. Missed Savings is forward-looking: at current prices, what would switching supplier be worth? Use the first to justify the tool, the second to find work to do.

If you get stuck

Missed Savings needs matched lists to exist. Without them you get a Price comparison not available card and a Go to Product Matching button — which, if you're in All Locations mode, bounces you straight back to the dashboard. Pick a restaurant first.

Drilling in

13

Watching orders across the group

History, drafts and things that failed
StatusWhat it means
DraftBuilt but never submitted; expires 14 days after it was last opened
Price ChangedA supplier moved the price after the cart was built; waiting on a decision
Waiting to Submit / ProcessingIn the queue or being placed with the supplier
Completed / ConfirmedPlaced successfully
ReceivedSomeone marked it as physically delivered
FailedPlacement failed; the row shows why, and can be retried
Watch out

Three things reliably confuse people here. The KPI cards at the top always mean “completed orders in the range” and ignore the status filter. Open work — drafts, failures, price changes — is always shown regardless of the date range. And cancelled orders are hidden unless you filter for them explicitly.

14

Placing an order as the owner

Same flow your chefs use

Owners are operators, so you can order exactly as a chef does. The one difference is that you must pick a specific restaurant first — the New Order button stays greyed in All Locations mode.

  1. Pick a restaurant, then + NEW ORDER.
  2. Choose an order list or the full matched list.
  3. Set quantities. Click any supplier's cell to override the automatic best-price choice.
  4. Watch the per-supplier minimum meters in the navy bar at the bottom.
  5. Set a delivery date, then Create Orders.
Tip

Create Orders stays disabled until you have both at least one item and a delivery date. A supplier under its minimum blocks only itself — the big submit button relabels to Submit 1 of 2 Orders and lets the good order through.

Tip

The full chef walkthrough — reading catch-weight rows, CS/PC toggles, out-of-stock behaviour and the mobile builder — is in The Chef's Guide. It applies to you unchanged.

15

Order lists and Price Check

The two shortcuts worth teaching your team

Lists are reusable templates — no quantities, no prices, just the products you buy on a given day or for a given station. Because they're shared per restaurant, whatever you build is what your chefs will open on their next shift.

  • The magnifier in the top nav opens it; type three or more characters.
  • Pick a destination list under Add to: and press Add on any result.
  • It's owner and chef only — managers don't get the icon.
16

EnPlace Pro on your phone

A different interface, not a shrunken one

On a phone the app serves purpose-built screens with a three-tab bottom bar — Home, Order, Cart — and no top navigation at all.

If you get stuck

That greyed-out tab bar is the mobile version of the All Locations block, and it's the single most confusing thing about the phone app. Tapping does nothing at all — no toast, no redirect. Pick a specific restaurant in the dashboard dropdown and both tabs come back.

Everything that isn't Home, Order or Cart lives behind the avatar circle at the top right of the dashboard: Settings, Team, Billing, Restaurants, Suppliers, Order History and Product Search.

Watch out

Mobile order cards don't show which restaurant an order belongs to. In All Locations mode orders from both sites interleave with nothing to tell them apart until you open one.

17

Billing and subscription

What the plan covers, and where seats actually live
  • Manage Billing hands off to Stripe for cards, addresses and receipts.
  • Cancel Subscription schedules cancellation at the end of the period — a yellow panel then offers Reactivate Subscription until it takes effect.
  • Invoice history links to Stripe's hosted invoice and PDF.
  • A failed payment shows a Payment failed banner across the top of every page until it's fixed.
Watch out

Seat usage is not on this screen. It's in the header of the Team screen (“4/5 seats included”). Billing shows the plan; Team shows the headcount driving it.

Who can do this

Only owners can act here. A manager or chef who reaches the URL can see the plan and invoices but every button redirects them away.

18

Keeping it healthy

The short list of things that actually go wrong

1. A supplier connection breaks

This is the most common failure by a wide margin, and it's silent from the ordering side — a price column simply disappears from the builder. Your dashboard alert is the early warning.

MessageFix
Session expiredNormal on 2FA suppliers. Validate, enter the new code.
Credentials are no longer validThe password changed at the supplier. Edit the credential.
Account on holdCall the supplier — nothing in the app will fix this.
Validation failedRead the detail; often a temporary supplier-side outage. Retry.

2. Someone can't reach a page

SymptomCause
Bounced to the dashboard with a “select a specific restaurant” messageAll Locations mode. Pick a restaurant.
A manager says buttons don't workThey're read-only on operations. Expected.
A chef can't see ReportsChefs never get Reports. Expected.
Edit controls missing on a matched listIt's promoted org-wide, so it's read-only. Demote to edit.

3. Account settings

Watch out

Every change on this screen requires your current password, even a typo fix in your name. And Delete my account removes you, not the organization — as the sole owner, that is effectively unrecoverable.
